event: Mitre consultant report on 2004 Florida hurricanes
text: [paraphrase] found FEMA lacked clear HQ-to-field leadership, ran outdated plans, needed better-trained staff, and could not get a clear picture of unfolding emergencies.
Also, FEMA personnel and state and local responders expressed confusion and frustration because FEMA's logistics system lacks an asset visibility program.
During Hurricane Katrina, this information was fragmented and dispersed among multiple systems.
[paraphrase] repeated the same four failures the 2005 Mitre report had named; FEMA pulled the review from its website after a reporter asked about it.

text: Difficulties experienced during the response directly correlate with weaknesses in FEMA's grant programs, staffing, training, catastrophic planning, and remediation of issues identified during previous disasters and exercises.
